findings.title: Malformed review status becomes a successful 'None recorded' claim
findings.problem: The completeness check accepts every string as a review status. For a measure with status Waiting, versions [{version: 1, status: Declined, context_revision: 2, design_version: 3}, {version: 2, status: Waiting, context_revision: 2, design_version: 3}], and review {status: 'garbled', decision_version: 1}, _complete returns True, _review_version returns None because the status is not exactly 'Needs human review', _held returns None, and _summaries writes 'None recorded' in the retained-review column. This is a deterministic static trace, not an executed reproduction. Existing measure_decision_view deep-copies resident_reviews into the projection without validating this status (resident_decisions.py:1058), so the malformed value can reach this serializer. The existing writer supplies 'Needs human review' or 'Reviewed with supplied acceptance' (resident_decisions.py:1619-1624); arbitrary strings do not establish that no review is retained. Admission Q6 explicitly forbids incomplete evidence becoming None recorded, and the UI note makes that an absence claim. Existing malformed-evidence tests cover a non-dict review and a dict missing status, but not an unrecognized string status. This defeats one of the explicit fail-closed admission conditions.
findings.current_code: and (review is None or (isinstance(review, dict) and isinstance(review.get("status"), str)))
findings.suggested_fix: Validate review.status against the actual existing projection vocabulary ('Needs human review', 'Reviewed with supplied acceptance') rather than accepting every string. Preserve explicit None as no review. Route missing/unknown/non-string statuses in a review object to UNAVAILABLE, not None recorded. Add serializer and HTTP projection tests with empty/unknown review-status strings and a retained Declined followed by Waiting; assert Unknown and no false None recorded, while valid reviewed acceptance still works. Do not change Core.
